title: Agent-side hunch_task calls are conditional: the prompt hook prints the verify command, and finish is called only when the task used Hunch
context: Measured on 2026-09-19 sessions: hunch_task start+finish cost ~87 main-session model calls per day (~6% of the main model's context re-reads), almost all returning an empty report ('No task-linked delivery observed'). The Stop hook already closes the task unconditionally (closeHookTask) and shows the report when non-empty (stopHookReport), and the only reason the hook text demanded a start call was to obtain verification_argv. Decided by David on 2026-09-20 via an inline question (three options offered; he chose the conditional contract).
decision: On hosts with a prompt hook, the hook's task instruction prints the exact `task verify <task_id> --` launcher inline, so the model no longer calls hunch_task start. The model calls hunch_task finish (and pastes the contribution card) only when the task used Hunch: a hunch_* call made with the task_id, a task-verify check, or an application to claim. Otherwise it skips finish; the host Stop hook closes the task as a host close and renders the evidence when the report is non-empty. Hosts without prompt hooks keep start + finish. start still works and still returns verification_argv. If the launcher cannot be computed the hook falls back to the old start-call wording (fail open).
consequences: The contribution card appears in the final response only for tasks that used Hunch; an untouched task leaves an empty ledger row closed by the host.
The verify launcher printed by the hook is the hook's installation, which is the same exact-pinned version as the MCP server's.
Generated CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md blocks, the MCP server instructions and the hunch_task tool description all state the same conditional contract, phrased client-agnostically.
alternatives_rejected: Drop only the start call and keep finish mandatory: halves the calls, but every prompt that never touched Hunch still pays a model round-trip to fetch an empty card the Stop hook would not even print.
Leave both calls mandatory: keeps the visibility contract untouched but keeps paying ~87 full-context model calls a day for empty reports.
Remove the agent-side finish entirely and rely on the Stop hook alone: loses agent-reported applications and the card inside the final response, which the host-side notice cannot supply.
